raw_response:
I will farm the 2.6 mu the same way I usually do, wheat first and then summer maize on the same land, but I will keep the fertilizer a little on the safe side because land is small and I cannot afford a bad yield. I have well water, so I do not need to depend only on rain. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put most fertilizer in before sowing, and then topdress once around jointing. Wheat in my area needs steady water, so I will irrigate about 3 times if the season is normal. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep the stand neat, put base fertilizer plus one topdressing, and water about 2 times if rain is not enough. I have farmed 20 years, so I do not like making big changes. I usually look at what fields around me do, then I adjust a little by my own money and water conditions. Since my farm is only 2.6 mu, I will spend enough on fertilizer and seed, but I will not go too fancy. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain.
